title: Exhaustion regex: harden the legacy (usage|weekly) branch anchoring + close the codex/agy verb-drift blind spot
notes: Follow-ups from the adversarial review of the 2026-07-26 'hit your weekly limit' drift fix (5th-gen wording; cycles 1077-1096 exit-81 livelock). (1) MEDIUM: claude-tmux's legacy branch `(?:reached|hit) your (usage|weekly) limit` carries no second-person anchor and no companion requirement — unlike the hardened per-model branch — so third-person prose like 'a cache hit your usage limit and fell back' false-matches (parity-preserving with the old 'reached' risk envelope, but now two verbs wide). Consider requiring the second-person chrome OR a companion (`/usage-credits` next-line tolerant, or the `· resets` suffix) and pin both verbs' prose guards in notWalls. (2) codex-tmux and agy-tmux exhausted_regex only match 'limit reached'/'quota (exceeded|reached)' era wordings — if either CLI drifts to a 'hit your ... limit' form they inherit the identical exit-81-instead-of-85 blind spot; add real-pane-derived fixtures + wording-drift regression locks per manifest (the claude-tmux test file is the template). Remember the self-trigger guard: fixtures must be concatenation-split so Read-tool cat-n renderings of the test source cannot match the live regex.
